name: Noel Emery
life: “I still remember transplanting a rose from a neighbor's closing shop.” On Sunday, near Breakwater Way, Noel stops on the landward side of the cycle track to watch the first boats turn for home.
voice: I can move one rosebush and cannot promise it will flower again. I told both owners before taking a spade to it.
appearance: Out of work clothes, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. Noel has heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Noel presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Noel enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Noel is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To move only rosebushes capable of surviving.
family: Daniel Fraser is Noel’s cousin’s child. Noel is free to hang up first. Daniel makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Reopening at six*, Daniel says, “I am the teenager everyone expects to cover late.”
connections: Marco Lam. A path for a walking frame has to coexist with the rose that may not survive moving.

reactions.situation: A grandchild objects to the garden plan
reactions.response: Noel asks the household members who will use the garden how they want to live in it now.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Noel asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
